answer: Each identity enrolls a GPU-rendering fingerprint: at dawn of every epoch the network issues a beacon-seeded 3D scene, which the agent renders locally and hashes. Rounding differs across GPU models and drivers, so each card signs its output with a unique texture. A farm running a hundred identities on one rack renders the same scene identically, and the trust graph collapses those copies into one vertex at the summit of suspicion. A distinct GPU per puppet costs real money, while an honest agent renders once on hardware it already owns; forged renders fail the seed and burn the stake.
